abstract: Undifferentiated embryonal carcinoma cells (EC cells) in the embryoid bodies isolated from mouse teratocarcinoma contained nucleolus-like bodies (NLBs) of smaller sizes in their cytoplasm (their sectional area averaged about 0.036 micrometers2). At the onset of EC cell differentiation, the average sectional area of NLBs significantly increased (about 0.107 micrometers2). When EC cells had differentiated into mesenchymal cells and endothelial cells of primitive blood vessels, NLBs decreased dramatically both in size and number. The possible role of NLBs in the differentiation process of EC cells is discussed.
abstract_ja: マウス奇形癌から単離した胚様体に含まれる未分化の胎児性癌細胞（EC細胞）は、細胞質内に小型の核小体様構造（NLB）を有していた（切断面の平均面積は約0.036μm²）。EC細胞の分化が始まると、NLBの平均切断面積は有意に増大した（約0.107μm²）。EC細胞が間葉系細胞や原始血管の内皮細胞へ分化すると、NLBは大きさと数の両面で著しく減少した。EC細胞の分化過程におけるNLBの役割について考察する。
